text: 主张白话也能作诗的胡适，其实自称是个保守的人，常对朋友说，语言文字是世界上最保守的东西，比宗教还保守。他最坚定的对手是梅光迪，此时在哈佛随一位保守派文学批评家深造；胡适说，正是梅光迪的强烈反对，把他“逼上梁山”。另一位是在康乃尔的朋友任鸿隽，他曾作打油诗取笑胡适，湖上那首纪事诗也出自他手。

Hu, the man arguing that it could, called himself a conservative. He used to tell his friends that language and writing are the most conservative things in the world, more conservative than religion. His most determined opponent was Mei Guangdi, then studying at Harvard under a conservative literary critic; it was Mei's fierce opposition, Hu later said, that drove him to Liangshan, the Chinese saying for being forced into a rebel's course against one's will. The other was Ren Hongjun, a friend at Cornell who once teased Hu in comic verse, and who had written the poem about the lake.
他对那首纪事诗的批评，引来一场风波。任鸿隽对“死语”的说法愤愤不平；更激动的是梅光迪，他路见不平，写来一封信猛烈反击。按胡适的说法，梅光迪那时正受他那位保守派老师的影响，对胡适的一切激进主张都反对到底。他认为文字必须经过第一流诗人的锻炼和美化，才能成为诗的文字。

His criticism of the lake poem set off a storm of its own. Ren was indignant about the dead words. Mei, angrier still, rushed to his friend's defence with a heated letter. By Hu's account, Mei was then under the influence of his conservative teacher and opposed everything radical Hu proposed. Words become poetic language, he insisted, only after first-rate poets have refined and beautified them.
